msgs: Water at a trail angel's water cache. Not on any map. Thank you, whoever keeps it running.
Found a trail angel's water cache the map doesn't show. Green and full of bugs. Filtered two litres anyway.
Thunderstorms forecast for tomorrow afternoon and a pass above treeline. Alarm set for an alpine start.
Afternoon storms again tomorrow. Up early, over the high stuff by noon: that's the rule up here.
Hail and lightning on the exposed part. Nowhere to hide up there, so I just kept moving, fast, down to the first trees.
Caught above treeline when the storm hit. Hair standing up, poles buzzing. Ran for the trees and didn't stop until I was well below the ridge.
Thunder right overhead on the high stretch, the gap between flash and boom down to a second. Crouched on my pad between strikes, then moved fast.
JUNCTION CREEK. The trailhead sign and the end of the Colorado Trail. Walked here from Denver. Now 3.5 miles of road into Durango for a burrito.
Took the Collegiate West: 79 miles instead of 77 on the main line (2 more).
Willow Fire closed 9 miles of trail. Hitched around it.
Day 1. Dropped at the Waterton Canyon trailhead south of Denver. Six miles of dirt road and bighorn sheep, then the real trail solo. Durango is 486 miles away.
Willow Fire closed 9 miles of trail. Road-walking the official detour.
Durango. The trailhead is 3.5 miles up Junction Creek, and the snow report for Kennebec Pass is the only thing anyone at the hostel talks about.
Waterton Canyon. The sign, a bighorn sheep watching, and the parking lot. Walked here from Durango.
Dry camp, and not enough water for dinner. Ate cold tortillas and went to bed thirsty.
Forecast says a big storm tomorrow. Big day today to get over the high country before it hits.
Back on the main CT after the Collegiate West.
Lightning on the ridge ahead. Not worth it. Waited in the forest with two other hikers until it blew over.
Thunderheads building over the pass. Stopped below treeline and waited it out under the trees, counting seconds between flash and boom.
Day 1. Cab from Durango to the Junction Creek trailhead. Signed the register and started up the creek toward Denver solo. Kennebec Pass tomorrow.
